lemmas.title: Mantel's Theorem (1907): every triangle-free simple graph on n vertices has at most n² / 4 edges
lemmas.statement:
Erdos.Claims.E_tur_001.mantel_theorem :
  ∀ (n : Nat) (G : Erdos.SimpleGraph n), ¬Erdos.HasTriangle G → 4 * Erdos.edgeCount G ≤ n * n
lemmas.registered_statement: ∀ (n : Nat) (G : SimpleGraph n), ¬ HasTriangle G → 4 * edgeCount G ≤ n * n
lemmas.verified_signature:
Erdos.Claims.E_tur_001.mantel_theorem :
  ∀ (n : Nat) (G : Erdos.SimpleGraph n), ¬Erdos.HasTriangle G → 4 * Erdos.edgeCount G ≤ n * n
lemmas.paper_notes: Induction removing both endpoints of an edge (u, v): since G is triangle-free, deg(u) + deg(v) ≤ n!

audit.notes: PR #4 cross-model audit: universal strong-induction proof of Mantel theorem 4 * edgeCount G ≤ n * n for all n and triangle-free G.

lemmas.registered_statement: (∃ col : Fin 4 → Fin 2, IsSumFreeColoring 4 2 col) ∧ SchurForced 5 2
lemmas.paper_notes: Coloring {1,4} vs {2,3} avoids x+y=z on {1..4}; on {1..5} forced by finite case check.

audit.notes: PR #1 cross-model audit: proves both 2-color sum-free witness on {1..4} and forced triple on {1..5}.

lemmas.title: Erdős #128 Bipartite Base Case: every bipartite graph on n vertices satisfies HasSparseHalf (an independent half of size ≥ n/2 has 0 ≤ n²/50 edges)
lemmas.statement:
Erdos.Claims.E_erd128_001.bipartite_has_sparse_half :
  ∀ (n : Nat) (G : Erdos.SimpleGraph n), Erdos.IsBipartite G → Erdos.HasSparseHalf G
lemmas.registered_statement: ∀ (n : Nat) (G : SimpleGraph n), IsBipartite G → HasSparseHalf G
lemmas.verified_signature:
Erdos.Claims.E_erd128_001.bipartite_has_sparse_half :
  ∀ (n : Nat) (G : Erdos.SimpleGraph n), Erdos.IsBipartite G → Erdos.HasSparseHalf G
lemmas.paper_notes: In any 2-coloring of G, the larger color class S has size ≥ n/2 and 0 internal edges, giving 50 * 0 ≤ n².

audit.notes: PR #4 cross-model audit: proves every bipartite graph on n vertices satisfies HasSparseHalf via larger color class.

lemmas.paper_notes: Blow-ups of C5 are the extremal tight family for Erdős Problem #128 (density 1/50 on halves).

lemmas.title: Erdős #156 Blocking Lemma: if A is a maximal Sidon subset of {1..N}, every x ∈ {1..N} \ A satisfies either x + a = b + c or 2x = a + b for some a, b, c ∈ A
lemmas.statement:
Erdos.Claims.E_erd156_001.maximal_sidon_blocking :
  ∀ (N : Nat) (A : List Nat) (x : Nat),
  Erdos.IsMaximalSidon N A →
    1 ≤ x →
      x ≤ N → ¬x ∈ A → (∃ a, a ∈ A ∧ ∃ b, b ∈ A ∧ ∃ c, c ∈ A ∧ x + a = b + c) ∨ ∃ a, a ∈ A ∧ ∃ b, b ∈ A ∧ x + x = a + b
lemmas.registered_statement: ∀ N A x, IsMaximalSidon N A → 1 ≤ x → x ≤ N → x ∉ A → (∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, ∃ c ∈ A, x + a = b + c) ∨ (∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, x + x = a + b)
lemmas.verified_signature:
Erdos.Claims.E_erd156_001.maximal_sidon_blocking :
  ∀ (N : Nat) (A : List Nat) (x : Nat),
  Erdos.IsMaximalSidon N A →
    1 ≤ x →
      x ≤ N → ¬x ∈ A → (∃ a, a ∈ A ∧ ∃ b, b ∈ A ∧ ∃ c, c ∈ A ∧ x + a = b + c) ∨ ∃ a, a ∈ A ∧ ∃ b, b ∈ A ∧ x + x = a + b
lemmas.paper_notes: Foundation of the Ω(N^{1/3}) lower bound on maximal Sidon sets (Erdős–Sós–Sárközy, Problem #156): every excluded x must collide in sum with A.

audit.notes: PR #3 cross-model audit: genuinely proves maximal Sidon blocking property for arbitrary N, A, x.

lemmas.title: Erdős #156 Small-N Synthesis: construct and Lean-verify a maximal Sidon subset A ⊆ {1..30} of size at most 6
lemmas.registered_statement: ∃ A : List Nat, A.length ≤ 6 ∧ IsMaximalSidon 30 A
lemmas.paper_notes: Use Python/SAT search to synthesize a maximal Sidon subset of {1..30} with |A| ≤ 6 (note greedy gives size 7: {1,2,4,8,13,21,31}!), then verify IsMaximalSidon 30 A in Lean 4!

audit.notes: PR #3 cross-model audit: exhibits genuine 5-element maximal Sidon set [1,4,11,15,17] in {1..30} (stronger than ≤ 6).

lemmas.title: Erdős #128 Exact n=10 Sharpness: exhibit a triangle-free 10-vertex graph (e.g. C5[2] or Petersen) achieving 50·e(S) ≥ 100 on every ≥5-vertex half and exact equality 50·e(S) = 100
lemmas.paper_notes: Replaces flagged E-erd128-002 (n=5). True 1/50 sharpness first occurs at n=10: C5[2] or Petersen has min_{|S|>=5} e(S) = 2 so 50*2 = 100 = n^2. Import Erdos.Statements.E_erd128_003 and state your theorem literally as `: Erdos.Statements.E_erd128_003.Claim`.

lemmas.title: Erdős #156 Exact Minimum at N=30: prove no maximal Sidon subset of {1..30} has size ≤ 4 (pinning exact min = 5 with E-erd156-002)
lemmas.paper_notes: By E-erd156-001 every x in {1..30}\A must collide in sum with A; a 4-element set can block at most 26 elements including itself (count distinct a+b-c and (a+b)/2!). Import Erdos.Statements.E_erd156_003 and state `: Erdos.Statements.E_erd156_003.Claim`.

lemmas.title: Exact Schur Number S(3) = 13 Upper Bound: every 3-coloring of {1..14} contains a monochromatic Schur triple x + y = z
lemmas.paper_notes: Closes exact S(3) = 13! Break color symmetry (WLOG col(1)=0, col(2)=1), then branch cleanly (or embed a tiny verified DRAT/case-split tree in pure Lean 4). Import Erdos.Statements.E_sch_004 and state `: Erdos.Statements.E_sch_004.Claim`.

lemmas.title: Exact Ramsey R(3,4) = 9 Upper Bound: every 9-vertex simple graph has a 3-independent set or a 4-clique
lemmas.paper_notes: Closes exact R(3,4)=9! By handshaking lemma, a 9-vertex graph cannot be 3-regular, so some vertex has degree ≥ 4 (apply R(3,3)=6 or neighbor clique) or non-degree ≥ 6.

lemmas.title: Paley-17 Witness for R(4,4) > 17: exhibit a 17-vertex graph with neither K4 nor a 4-independent set
lemmas.paper_notes: Connect u and v in Z/17Z iff (u - v) mod 17 is a nonzero quadratic residue {1,2,4,8,9,13,15,16}. Self-complementary so K4-free implies Indep4-free!

lemmas.title: Circulant Witness for R(3,5) > 13: exhibit a 13-vertex triangle-free graph with no 5-independent set
lemmas.paper_notes: Circulant graph on Z/13Z with edge differences {1, 5, 8, 12} (cubic residues / C_13(1,5)) is triangle-free and has independence number 4.

lemmas.title: Avoidance Construction for R(3,6) > 17: exhibit a 17-vertex triangle-free graph with no 6-independent set
lemmas.paper_notes: Use SAT/circulant search on Z/17Z (e.g. step set {1, 3, 8, 9, 14, 16}? Verify triangle-free & alpha ≤ 5!) then verify in pure Lean 4.

lemmas.title: Erdős #156 Exact Length-5 Witness at N=30: prove ∃ A, A.length = 5 ∧ IsMaximalSidon 30 A (closing exact min = 5 with E-erd156-003)
lemmas.paper_notes: Closes the catalog signature gap: E-erd156-002 proved length ≤ 6 using [1,4,11,15,17]; certify length = 5 directly against the frozen statement.

lemmas.title: Erdős #156 Universal Ω(N^{1/3}) Barrier: prove N ≤ |A| + |A|³ for EVERY maximal Sidon subset A ⊆ {1..N}
lemmas.paper_notes: Every x in {1..N}\A is either b+c-a (a,b,c in A) or (a+b)/2 (a<b in A); counting distinct blocked values bounds N - |A| ≤ |A|^3 for all N and A.

lemmas.title: Erdős #156 N=100 Synthesis: construct and Lean-verify a maximal Sidon subset of {1..100} of size ≤ 8 (beating greedy size 10)
lemmas.paper_notes: Greedy gives size 10; randomized/SAT search finds size 8 (e.g. [5,46,48,56,57,60,76,82]) — verify IsMaximalSidon 100 A cleanly in pure Lean 4.

lemmas.title: FRONTIER CONTEST (Erdős #156 at N=100): Does {1..100} admit a maximal Sidon subset of size ≤ 7? Prove OR refute!
lemmas.paper_notes: Open search contest: either synthesize a 7-element maximal Sidon set in {1..100} OR prove ¬ Claim (all maximal Sidon sets in {1..100} have size ≥ 8).

lemmas.title: Schur Lower Bound S(4) ≥ 44: explicit 4-color sum-free coloring of {1..44} verified in Lean 4
lemmas.paper_notes: Exact S(4) = 44 (Baumert 1965): find a sum-free 4-coloring of {1..44} via SAT or classic construction and verify IsSumFreeColoring 44 4 col in Lean 4.

lemmas.title: Exact Van der Waerden W(3,3) = 9: {1..8} admits a 3-AP-free 2-coloring while every 2-coloring of {1..9} contains a monochromatic 3-AP
lemmas.paper_notes: Witness on {1..8}: 0,0,1,1,0,0,1,1; forced 3-AP on {1..9} proved by small branching tree over 2-colorings.

lemmas.title: 3-Color Van der Waerden Lower Bound W(3; 3) > 26: explicit 3-coloring of {1..26} with no monochromatic 3-term arithmetic progression
lemmas.paper_notes: W(3; 3) = 27 is exact; synthesize a 26-element 3-AP-free 3-coloring via SAT and verify IsAPFree3 26 3 col in Lean 4.
